record.paper_title: Current Open Questions in Complete Mixability
record.original_question: If C is a convex subset of ℝ^d, is the uniform distribution on C necessarily n-completely mixable for every n ≥ d + 1?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5. Is a uniform distribution on a convex set C ⊂ R^d necessarily n-CM for all n > d + 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d \geq 1$ be an integer and let $C \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a convex set of finite, positive Lebesgue measure. Let $X$ be a random vector uniformly distributed on $C$, with mean $\mu = \mathbb{E}[X] \in \mathbb{R}^d$. For an integer $n \geq 2$, the distribution of $X$ is said to be $n$-completely mixable ($n$-CM) if there exist random vectors $X_1, \dots, X_n$, each having the same distribution as $X$ (i.e., uniform on $C$), defined on a common probability space, such that
$$X_1 + X_2 + \cdots + X_n = n\mu \quad \text{almost surely.}$$

Question: Is it true that for every convex set $C \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ of finite positive volume, the uniform distribution on $C$ is $n$-completely mixable for every integer $n \geq d+1$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches on complete mixability literature (Puccetti–Wang and successors) surface general results — e.g. continuous distributions with concave densities are $n$-CM for all $n\geq 2$, and $n$-radially symmetric distributions are $m$-CM for $m\geq n+1$ — but no source verifying or refuting the specific claim that the uniform law on an arbitrary convex body in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is $n$-CM for all $n \geq d+1$ was found. The current status appears unresolved in the publicly available literature.

status_evidence.title: Advances in Complete Mixability (Puccetti, Wang, Wang, JAP 2012)
status_evidence.snippet: Provides characterizations of n-CM distributions including concave densities and radial symmetry, but does not settle the convex-set uniform conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Background results on n-CM but no resolution of the d+1 question for uniform distributions on convex sets.

status_evidence.title: Sums of Standard Uniform Random Variables
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses joint mixability problems for uniform marginals; complete determination of feasible joint distributions remains unclear in dimension n=2.
status_evidence.claim: Related uniform-mixability questions remain partially open.
